transcript:
Meeting: AstraGenomics - POC scoping (open models)
Date: 2026-10-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Park (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Ravi Shah (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Lena Ward (AstraGenomics, Head of ML), Markus Chen (CTO), Tina Ko (Data Eng), Oliver Ng (Research Lead)
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20261021-astrag-8421 (placeholder)

Summary: agree on POC goals: model quality (genomics QA/NER), latency target <250ms p95 for single-turn inference, throughput ~60 reqs/sec during peak, and evaluation metrics (EM/F1 for extraction tasks, Rouge for summarization). Plan is a 4-week POC: week 1 data prep & access; week 2 benchmarks with open models; week 3 optimizations (quant, batching, KV cache); week 4 final report and decision.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Sophie Park: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm sophie from Redwood. quick roll call?
[00:08] Dr. Lena Ward: hi lena here, thanks for setting this up.
[00:11] Markus Chen: markus here.
[00:12] Tina Ko: tina, thanks.
[00:15] Miguel Alvarez: miguel from redwood se, happy to dig into perf and benchmarks.
[00:20] Sophie Park: cool, the agenda — success criteria, sizing, models, benchmarks, timeline. lena, do you want to start with your goals for the POC?
[00:30] Dr. Lena Ward: yeah, we want to evaluate open models for two main workloads: 1) named entity extraction and relation extraction from clinical notes and genomic reports, and 2) concise summarization of variant annotation results. must work on multi-lingual records (english + spanish + japanese occasionally). accuracy is top priority but cost matters — we can't blow up inference spend.
[01:05] Markus Chen: and from ops perspective we have to prove we can keep data in our VPC, or at least ensure KMS-managed keys for encryption. SOC2 docs are required.
[01:18] Sophie Park: that makes sense, we can support both hosted and private — for POC usually we run benchmarks on hosted with a dedicated pool, or run the Redwood Private trial in your VPC if you'd prefer. any preference?
[01:35] Tina Ko: we'd prefer private for the final system but ok to do initial benchmarking hosted as long as data is anonymized.
[01:42] Miguel Alvarez: noted. on modeling — based on your tasks i would shortlist several open models: Llama 2 13B finetuned variants, Mistral-Instruct style 7B/7B+, and a couple of LLMs optimized for long context like MosaicML/Redwood-verified variants. the tradeoff is size vs quality vs cost; larger models give better F1 on extraction but cost more and need quantization strategy.
[02:20] Oliver Ng: last time we ran something similar with a 13B it did okay on extraction but hallucinated on relations — how do you avoid that?
[02:28] Miguel Alvarez: good q. for structured extraction we recommend a few strategies: 1) prompt templates with example-driven extraction + validation, 2) light-weight finetune or instruction-tuning on a small annotation set (few hundred examples), or 3) use a hybrid approach: a smaller dense model for classification + a specialized NER pipeline. we'll benchmark both generation-based extraction and a supervised classifier baseline.
[03:05] Dr. Lena Ward: timeline? how long to run a meaningful benchmark?
[03:10] Sophie Park: typically 2 weeks of active benchmarking: 3-5 model variants, multiple quantization levels (int8, int4 where supported), and with your representative dataset. then 1-2 weeks for optimizations. overall 4 weeks is standard for a POC.
[03:26] Markus Chen: ok what's the expected throughput? our peak is about 60 reqs/sec for extraction and 20 reqs/sec for summarize bursts.
[03:36] Miguel Alvarez: fine — we'll size test infra for 100 concurrent qps so we cover headroom. cost estimates will vary: a Llama-13B in int8 on dedicated GPUs is cheaper per-token than float16 on multi-node setups; we'll include unit economics in the proposal.
[03:55] Tina Ko: multilingual — do the models support spanish/japanese out of box or do we need special finetunes?
[04:02] Miguel Alvarez: many open models have decent multilingual coverage in common languages, spanish is usually fine; japanese can be hit-or-miss — we'll include specific evals per language. if needed we can do lightweight finetune with your annotated examples.
[04:20] Sophie Park: success criteria: lena, can you give the targets?
[04:25] Dr. Lena Ward: ideally for NER we want F1 > 0.87 on our holdout; relation extraction F1 > 0.80; summarization rouge-l > 0.60 but more qualitative. latency should be p95 < 250ms for extraction in single-turn mode, and p95 < 500ms for summarization (since it may be longer). cost target — we don't want to exceed $0.02 per extraction average. those are rough but give us a baseline.
[05:02] Sophie Park: great — we'll use those as pass/fail thresholds for the POC.
[05:08] Miguel Alvarez: benchmark plan: we will run 1) quality evals on holdout labeled set (EM/F1/Rouge), 2) performance perf tests (latency p50/p95, throughput), 3) resource utilization (GPU mem, token/sec), and 4) cost modeling with real token counts. we will test model variants: 7B-lingual, 13B, and a 30B if needed, with int8/int4 quantizations where supported.
[05:50] Oliver Ng: can you share the specific models you plan to test?
[05:54] Miguel Alvarez: yes, initial shortlist: Llama-2-13B-chat, Mistral-large-7B-instruct, Redw-13B-optim (our tuned open variant), and a long-context model like Llama-2-13B-extended or Mosaic-Long-16k. we'll put the precise hashes in the benchmark spreadsheet. note: some variants may require different kernel stacks for good perf.
[06:20] Dr. Lena Ward: are there known quality tradeoffs with quantization?
[06:25] Miguel Alvarez: yes, int8 usually keeps quality within 1-3% on F1; int4 can drop more and is model-dependent — we'll quantify this. for extraction tasks small drop may be acceptable if cost savings are large.
[06:40] Markus Chen: security again — you mentioned KMS and audit logs?
[06:44] Sophie Park: yes we support KMS integration for Private and Dedicated. audit logs and per-request tracing available in Redwood Console. i'll include SOC2 and our security whitepaper link in the follow-up.
[06:58] Tina Ko: on data — we'll sanitize PII but can share de-identified records. we will need NDAs in place for any raw data; can you sign?
[07:10] Sophie Park: yes we'll get legal looped if needed; standard NDA is fine.
[07:14] Miguel Alvarez: for benchmarks we prefer you drop samples to an S3 bucket we control access to or we can spin up a short-lived private endpoint in your VPC if you prefer.
[07:28] Dr. Lena Ward: S3 with pre-signed links works. we'll aim to get 500-1k labeled examples for extraction and ~200 for summarization.
[07:38] Sophie Park: perfect. technical question from ravi — how do we handle long clinical notes and memory?
[07:43] Ravi Shah: right — we often use long-context models or chunking + KV cache. Redwood runtime supports KV cache and continuous batching; for summarization we may chunk inputs and stitch outputs. Miguel, any perf notes?
[07:59] Miguel Alvarez: yes, long context increases memory and can impact throughput. we will benchmark with both native long-context models and chunked pipelines; we'll log tokenization overhead too. also we'll test prefix/KV cache effectiveness for repeated prompts.
[08:18] Oliver Ng: how will you measure hallucination rates?
[08:22] Miguel Alvarez: a combination of automated QA checks (fact matching against canonical database) and manual spot-checking. we'll generate a hallucination report as part of the quality analysis.
[08:35] Tina Ko: timeline recap?
[08:37] Sophie Park: week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and sign POC SOW; week 1: data ingest and access; week 2: run model benchmarks; week 3: optimizations and quant tests; week 4: final report and recommendations. target sign-off within 4 weeks.
[08:55] Markus Chen: cost — can you ballpark initial POC cost?
[08:59] Sophie Park: rough ballpark $8-12k for a hosted dedicated benchmarking run covering a few model variants; private trial may be higher due to infra setup. we'll include detailed TCO in proposal.
[09:12] Dr. Lena Ward: sounds reasonable. any blockers?
[09:15] Tina Ko: we need SOC2 and legal, and the dataset.
[09:18] Sophie Park: we'll send SOC2 + security docs, and the SOW.
[09:22] Miguel Alvarez: also we'll need expected token length distribution from you, to size batching properly — avg tokens per request and distribution percentiles.
[09:31] Dr. Lena Ward: yes we can provide token stats along with sample data.
[09:35] Sophie Park: ok last bit — reporting. we'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet with model rows, quant levels, metrics columns (p50/p95 latency, F1, cost per request), and an executive summary.
[09:50] Oliver Ng: will you also run a privacy analysis for on-prem?
[09:53] Sophie Park: yes, we'll map options: hosted with encryption-at-rest + KMS, Dedicated in customer VPC, and Private on-prem package. we'll outline risks and mitigations.
[10:05] Markus Chen: any specific infra prerequisites for a private trial?
[10:09] Miguel Alvarez: ideally a couple of GPUs if you want on-prem — we'll provide a sizing doc. for VPC we need peering or private endpoint and IAM roles for KMS.
[10:23] Dr. Lena Ward: fine. thanks everyone.
[10:27] Sophie Park: recap and next steps: sophie to send POC proposal + pricing, miguel to share benchmark plan and spreadsheet, tina to upload datasets, lena to confirm exact success thresholds. we'll schedule kickoff for week of 10/26.
[10:42] Tina Ko: sounds good, thanks.
[10:44] Sophie Park: great, i'll follow up after this call.
[44:30] [meeting ends]
